# Helping your midwife find you
## A warm welcome from Riverside Community Midwives

When you invite us into your home for your baby’s birth, you are welcoming us into a very special family moment. We want you to feel comfortable with us, whether this is your first baby or you have done it all before.

We also want to find your front door without a tour of Liverpool first.

A little planning now can save precious time on the day, especially at 3am, when the street is dark, the house numbers are hiding and the sat nav thinks your baby is arriving at the chippy.

Here is how you can help us reach you safely, with our bags, equipment and energy ready for you.

## First things first: when to call

**Riverside’s planned home birth cover starts at 37 weeks of pregnancy.**

If you think labour is starting **before 37 weeks**, call your maternity unit straight away. You will need hospital assessment and care rather than a planned home birth. Do not wait for home birth cover to begin.

**From 37 weeks, phone the Riverside birth line when you think labour is starting.** You do not need to be certain before calling. The midwife will talk with you about what is happening and agree the next steps.

Please use the birth line, **not your midwife’s personal mobile**. The birth line reaches the team member on call. Your usual midwife may be off duty, asleep or away from their phone.

Keep the birth line number saved in your phone and written on your fridge checklist. Use the number in your maternity notes or given to you by the team.

**Call rather than sending a message when labour starts or you need urgent advice.** A text, WhatsApp message or Facebook post may not be seen straight away.

If you cannot get through, follow the backup contact instructions in your maternity notes. Do not wait for a reply to a message if you need help.

**For a life-threatening emergency, call 999.** If your baby seems to be coming now and a midwife is not with you, call 999 and follow the call handler’s instructions.

## Tell us where you are — not just where the sat nav thinks you are

When you call, please give us:

- Your name.
- Your full address, including postcode.
- Your house or flat number, and the building name if there is one.
- A phone number we can reach you on.
- Any important directions or access details.

Even if we have visited before, please remind us about anything tricky. The midwife coming to your birth may be someone you have not met yet.

If your home has a name rather than a number, tell us what is nearby and where the entrance is. “Rosemary Cottage” sounds lovely, but it helps to know which gate belongs to Rosemary.

Please also tell us about roadworks, closed roads, one-way streets or an entrance that is around the back.

## Flats: help us solve the front-door puzzle

Flat numbers do not always follow the rules we expect. Flat 14 may be nowhere near flat 13. Sometimes it is in another building entirely.

If you live in a flat, please tell us:

- Which block or building to enter.
- Which entrance to use.
- Your floor and flat number.
- How the entry phone works.
- Whether there is a lift, and whether it is working.
- Any gate code or other access instructions we need.

Share entry codes directly with the team, **not in the Facebook group**.

If the buzzer is broken or your name is not on it, let us know. We would much rather have a clear plan than stand outside pressing buttons and hoping.

## Make your home easy to spot

Please check that your house number or name can be seen from the road. A number hidden behind a hedge is playing hide-and-seek rather too well.

**At night, switch on your porch or outside light if you have one.** A light inside a front window can also help. Please make sure the route to the door is well lit and safe.

A bright, easy-to-describe marker can be useful: for example, a ribbon or party decoration on the gate. Tell us what to look for, and secure it safely without blocking the entrance.

If someone is available, they could watch for us from a window or meet us at the entrance. But nobody needs to leave you alone to become a human lighthouse.

Please tell us which door to use. An open door on its own is not a reliable sign — we need to know we have the right home!

## A map pin can help too

A map pin or a what3words location can help us find a difficult entrance. Please check that it points to the **entrance we should use**, not the middle of the building or a neighbouring road.

Ask the team during pregnancy whether the birth line phone accepts WhatsApp location pins, and how they would like you to share one.

These are extra directions, not a replacement for your full address or a phone call. **Always call the birth line first when labour starts.**

## Parking: two midwives, quite a lot of luggage

Two midwives usually attend your birth, often in separate cars. If possible, please plan for **two nearby parking spaces**.

We bring more than a handbag: there may be gas and air cylinders, a large birth bag and other equipment. A shorter, clear route from the car helps us bring everything in safely.

If parking is difficult, tell us beforehand. We can discuss the nearest practical place to park and unload. Please do not put yourself at risk trying to save a space.

If you live in a permit zone, including parts of Anfield and Kensington, check the arrangements with the council before your due date. Visitor permits may need arranging in advance.

Have any permits ready and tell us how to use them. If a permit needs displaying on a dashboard, make sure it is available for us when we arrive. We still need to follow local parking rules — a midwife’s bag is sadly not a parking permit.

## A clear path for you and us

Please keep the entrance, hallway and stairs clear.

Shoes, washing baskets, bags and children’s toys can all become trip hazards when someone is carrying equipment. Lego is impressive stuff, but nobody wants to discover it underfoot during a birth.

You do **not** need a spotless house. We are coming to support you, not inspect your skirting boards. A clear, safe route matters much more than tidy cushions.

Plan how we will get in, but there is no need to leave your home unlocked while waiting. If your access arrangements change, tell us.

## Pets: much loved, safely settled

We know pets are part of the family. Some also feel strongly that every visitor has come especially to see them.

Please settle pets in another secure room before we arrive, away from the entrance and birth equipment. Arrange for someone to look after them if needed.

This helps prevent escapes, trips and enthusiastic greetings while we are carrying heavy kit. We love a friendly dog. We just need both hands for the gas and air.

## Your fridge checklist

### Helping Riverside find us

☐ I know planned home birth cover starts at **37 weeks**.

☐ I have saved the **Riverside birth line** number.

**Birth line:** __________________________________

**Backup maternity contact:** _____________________

☐ My birth partner or support person knows to **call the birth line**, not a personal mobile.

☐ Our full address and postcode are ready to give.

**Address:** ____________________________________

________________________________________________

**Postcode:** ___________________________________

☐ We have written down any tricky directions, flat details or entry instructions.

**Entrance and access notes:** ____________________

________________________________________________

☐ Our house number or name is easy to see.

☐ We have a plan for lighting the entrance at night.

☐ We have checked parking for **two cars if possible**.

☐ Any visitor permits are ready.

☐ The doorway, hallway and stairs are clear.

☐ Pets have a safe, separate space.

☐ We have checked with the team how to share a location pin, if needed.

**You do not need a perfect home or a perfect plan. Tell us about any difficulties during pregnancy and we will work through them together. We are looking forward to meeting your baby — and finding your front door first time.**
